When Billie Burke stepped into the towering, star-studded tulle gown and floating pink bubble to play the seemingly ageless, ethereal Good Witch of the North, she was actually fifty-four years old and a deeply seasoned Hollywood veteran. Far from a naive fairy tale ingenue, Burke was a brilliant, highly accomplished comedic stage actress and the widow of the legendary theatrical producer Florenz Ziegfeld. Director Victor Fleming expertly utilized her immense, underlying maturity to ground the highly whimsical character. By delivering her famously breathy, high-pitched dialogue with a subtle, quietly commanding authority, Burke masterfully proves that the most enduring cinematic magic does not come from youth or simple visual spectacle, but from a fiercely experienced performer projecting a profound, unwavering warmth that instantly makes a terrifying new world feel completely safe.
⠀
The Wizard of Oz (1939), directed by Victor Fleming, starring Judy Garland, Frank Morgan, Billie Burke. A fiercely determined, deeply misunderstood farm girl is swept away by a terrifying, massive tornado to a breathtaking, highly dangerous magical land, where she must embark on a treacherous journey down a yellow brick road to find the one mysterious wizard who can finally send her home.
